#### BL-496 Two defects from #393's round-3 delta review: a late answer from an earlier account replaces the next account's answer, and Try again can show a passive error
- Status: done (PR #400, tests tagged BL-496 in `apps/mobile/test/account-deletion-gate-hook.test.ts`). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer (S14: lib/account-deletion and the deletion screen), qa engineer. Milestone: M9. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium. The delta review's one Should (PASS WITH NOTES, no Must); the coordinator waived it for build 2.
- Gate: waived for build 2 by the coordinator (30 Oct); before the next build that real families use with sign-in on.
- Satisfies: none given. Cited: C-REQ-019 (`docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md:224`).
- Problem and evidence (the round-3 delta review of #393, relayed by the coordinator; the code came with #393, merged as 146a8ff, and every cite was re-opened on that tree; both points are code reading and were not run: unverified):
  1. A late answer from an earlier account replaces the next account's answer. `askServer` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/account-deletion/use-first-run-gate.ts:59-73`) writes through `say` (`:60`), which resets the answer slot to the asking account whenever the slot belongs to another account. The read effect's cleanup only clears the cap timer (`:72`, `:104-107`), so a read that outlives its account still calls `say` when it ends, and the with-book read effect has no cleanup at all (`:112-116`). The sequence: A is signed in on a phone whose closed book is still local (`server_state='deleted'`); A's read stalls; A signs out and B signs in on the same Onboarding mount; B's read answers `none`, so B sees the welcome; A's stalled read then ends, even as a failure. The slot becomes `{ for: A, checked: true }`, `checked` is false for B, and `chooseScreen` answers `checking` for a signed-in phone with a closed book (`apps/mobile/src/lib/account-deletion/open-request.ts:239`). `CheckingScreen` has no button, not even Sign out (`apps/mobile/src/components/settings/open-deletion.tsx:99-111`), so B sees paper until the app is relaunched. It needs two accounts and a read that outlives the other's whole sign-in.
  2. Try again can show a passive error on the "Deletion cancelled" screen. `pressReducer` sets `acted` for any press, `retry` included (`apps/mobile/src/components/settings/open-deletion.logic.ts:39`), and the screen shows `failureLine(d.error)` once `acted` is set (`open-deletion.tsx:60`). The screen mounted offline after a cancel (the refresh set `error` to `offline`), the person taps Try again, and "Nothing has changed. Deleting an account needs a connection." (`errors.offline`, `packages/content/src/features/account-deletion.en.ts:107`) appears under "on their way back".
- Scope: (1) ignore a `say` whose `askedAs` is not the latest account asked (a ref set at the start of each ask), or keep the answers per account; (2) only a Cancel press sets `acted`.
- Done when: (1) a hook-level test with the stand-in (`apps/mobile/test/helpers/mini-react.ts`) shows A's late answer after B's leaves B's `checked` true, and it fails on the two mutations the review says survive today (the tag reset in `say` removed; the `askServer` cleanup removed); (2) a reducer test shows a `retry` press leaves `acted` false and a `cancel` press sets it.

#### BL-497 Device plan and run sheet fixes after #393: the S1-35 (d) wait, the S2-13 time, and the S1-35 Update line
- Status: done (docs only, branch `docs/qa-bl497-device-plan`: S1-35 (d) and its Update line in `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md`; block 8's time, the close, the end and the total in the T11 sheet; none of it run on a phone). Mode: agent. Owner: qa engineer. Milestone: M9. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Low. The founder runs these checks on staging; point 1 is Medium if the check is run before it is fixed.
- Gate: the build 2 checks session (`docs/qa/run-sheets/README.md:58`).
- Satisfies: none given.
- Problem and evidence (the round-3 delta review of #393, relayed by the coordinator; the plan lines are on `develop` since #393 added S1-35 at `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md:461`; this PR edits neither file, as the coordinator asked):
  1. S1-35 (d) (`docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md:467`) says that after the grant is restored "the phone's next sync brings the book back". The revoked grant makes `sync_pull` fail with 42501, which `classifyCallError` files under `server` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/errors.ts:33`). A failed pull only records `lastFailure` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/engine.ts:238-241`); the backoff (1 s, doubling to 5 minutes, `errors.ts:3-5`, `:37-39`) is written to the outbox's head op (`engine.ts:197`, `:219`), and `scheduleRetry` arms a timer only when an outbox op exists (`engine.ts:302-313`). A phone with an empty outbox has no retry timer: the next sync starts on a foreground (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/index.ts:235`, no sooner than 5 s after the last cycle, `engine.ts:91`, `:341`), on Try again (`syncNow`) or when the outbox changes. So the wording should tell the tester to send the app to the background and open it again, not to wait. Code reading, not run: unverified.
  2. The T11 session sheet gives S2-13 25 minutes (`docs/qa/run-sheets/2026-10-30-T11-session-1.md:63`, the 15:55 row), and #393's body estimates about 45 for S2-13 (a) to (h) with its base steps, and about 55 for S1-35 (20 of them a wait). The figures are in #393's body only; I found them in no file. Adding 20 minutes to the row moves the close and the total (the sheet states 7 h 15 min of device time against the 8-hour W2 budget, `:65`; my sum is 7 h 35 min, unverified against the sheet's other rows).
  3. S1-35's Update line (`DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md:482`) points at an S64 acceptance box, "a sole parent can reach Cancel deletion", that the spec does not contain: `docs/design/EXPERIENCE_PASS_2026-10.md` has four boxes (`:1633-1637`). The critics' section 5 gives that edit to the spec owner (BL-491 point 4).
- Scope: edit `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md` (points 1 and 3) and the T11 sheet (point 2), keeping the sheet's end time and total in step with the row.
- Done when: S1-35 (d) tells the tester to send the app to the background and open it again once the grant is back; the T11 row for S2-13 gives the time the plan needs, with the end time and the total following; the Update line names the box as proposed until the spec has it.

#### BL-499 Cancel deletion has no path on a phone that lists a book while the Delete account row is hidden
- Status: needs-decision (the founder confirms which Cancel path before it merges: options (a) and (b) show a row or a route again in a build where D-129 hides it, and option (c) adds a line outside the hidden page; no D-### or Q-### exists yet). Mode: pair. Owner: mobile engineer (S14: lib/account-deletion), qa engineer. Milestone: M9. Size: M. Depends on: none.

- Problem and evidence (re-opened on `develop` at e4fd94d; none run on a phone: unverified):
  1. The first-run gate answers `app` for any phone that lists a book, before it looks at a request: `if (phone.hasBook) return 'app';` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/account-deletion/open-request.ts:232`). Only a phone with no book reaches the open-request screen, which holds Cancel deletion and is not behind the switch (D-129 point 3).
  2. Every other phone cancels on Settings > Delete account (the button is labelled `c.scheduled.cancelButton` at `apps/mobile/src/app/settings/delete-account.tsx:152` and calls `d.cancel()` at `:154`). The row is drawn only when `capabilities.accountDeletion` is true (`apps/mobile/src/app/settings/index.tsx:116-122`) and `DeleteAccountRoute` redirects to Settings when it is false (`delete-account.tsx:57-58`).
  3. So with the variable off, three kinds of phone have an open request and no Cancel: a co-parent, a sole parent who also co-parents another book, and a sole parent before the closing pull arrives (the same three that D-129's Effects line names).
  4. How a phone gets there: a request can only be opened from a build where the row is on (a development client, or a build made with the variable on), so in practice the founder's drill accounts. #409's body accepts it for builds 1 and 2. That claim holds only while no support or email route can file a request. `docs/emails/CATALOG.md:116` lists `deletion-confirm`, a web link ("route still to build") that files a request with `source='support'` from any browser, and BL-500 option (b) would add a manual route for testers. Either would let a person on a hidden-row build have an open request, and widens who can be stranded.
- Scope: the founder confirms the path and the owner then builds it, saying why in the PR. (a) Keep the row and the route open on a phone that holds a local open-request note (the setting `accountDeletion.openRequest`, `open-request.ts:32`; `noteIsDead` decides when it no longer counts, `:187-198`), whatever the variable says: covers only a request made on this phone. (b) A status read from Settings (`loadStatus`, `apps/mobile/src/lib/account-deletion/api.ts:48`) that draws the row only when the server says a request is open: covers a request made on another phone, costs a read and needs offline words (content, and counsel, because it is a deletion term). (c) A path with no row, which #409's body names as "a Cancel path outside the hidden page": a line on Account or on Settings that appears only when a local open-request note or a server status read says a request is open, and that opens Cancel deletion. Same words and counsel rule as (b). Options (a) and (b) show a Delete account row or route in a build where D-129 hides it, and (c) shows another surface there, so all three differ from what D-129 hides; D-129 is not edited here.
- Done when: with the variable off, a test shows a phone that lists a book and has an open request reaches Cancel deletion, and a phone with no open request gets no new row, line or route; the pick and its reason are recorded here.

#### BL-502 Settings > Privacy's sync row follows the consent, not whether letters upload: five cases where it reads On or Off and the phone does something else
- Status: blocked (BL-485). Mode: agent. Owner: auth owner (S01), mobile engineer, content (words for any new status). Milestone: M5. Size: M. Depends on: BL-485.
- Priority: Low for build 2, which is family only; #408 recorded it as left open. Counsel relay item 29 (as the coordinator numbers it) covers points 1 and 2.
- Gate: with BL-485 option (a), before any friend outside the family signs in (D-128).
- Satisfies: none given. Cited: LEGAL-REQ-006 (P0, `docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md:63-67`).
- Problem and evidence (the row is `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/sensitive-row.ts:30-46`, from #408; its header says it follows the consent and not the claim screen, `:23-24`; every case is code reading, not run on a phone: unverified):
  1. On before the claim is answered. A signed-in phone with letters, before "Keep in this account" is answered: Privacy reads On (`ready`, `sync: 'on'`), Account reads "Not set up yet" (`apps/mobile/src/components/auth/account-view.logic.ts:39-42`), and nothing uploads (`syncAllowed()` is false while a claim is pending, `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/auth-store.ts:84-86`, `:98-100`).
  2. Account mismatch. `claim()` sets `mismatchUser` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/index.ts:178`), `ensureEngine` then never starts the engine (`:186-189`), and `:206` sets it again if `start()` fails. No Settings or Account line reads the `account_mismatch` phase (`:71`; only the join wait treats it as stalled, `apps/mobile/src/components/family/join-wait.logic.ts:34`), so the person is told nowhere, and both rows read On.
  3. Re-consent. `needsConsent` reads `off`, "Off, kept on this phone" (`sensitive-row.ts:39-40`; `packages/content/src/strings.en.ts:850`), also for a Terms-only or age-only re-consent while the sensitive-data consent still stands.
  4. No timer for `unknown`. `sync: 'unknown'` is read again on a foreground (`apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/session-provider.tsx:244-247`), on Try again (`refreshGate`, `:487`) and by the sign-out wait's 10 second poll (`:271-275`), and nowhere else.
  5. Two things that stop uploads never reach the row: the sync engine's `paused_consent` phase (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/engine.ts:142`) and the remote kill switch (`paused: syncKilled`, `sync/index.ts:200`). Neither changes `AuthState.sync`, so the row reads On while letters wait. BL-503 ends in this state: after its sequence the engine can sit in `paused_consent`, and the row still reads On.
- Scope: when BL-485 option (a) lands, the owner decides per point: the row follows a fuller state (a new status value, words by the content owner, counsel's read because it names a consent), or it is left as it is with the reason recorded. Points 1, 2 and 5 are about uploading, point 3 about the consent, point 4 about the clock.
- Done when: each point has a test against the real reducer (`apps/mobile/test/privacy-sensitive-row.test.ts` already runs it) that fails on its mutant, or is recorded here as left as it is; points 1 and 2 also have counsel's answer.

#### BL-503 Auth machine: answering Terms or the age line again turns sync on for a person who declined sensitive-data
- Status: done (PR #804, `apps/mobile/test/auth-machine.test.ts` case BL-503). Mode: agent. Owner: auth owner (S01), qa engineer. Milestone: M5. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium. Not new: the line dates from 3 Oct 2026 (`git blame`). The new Privacy row (#408) makes it visible.
- Gate: before the first build a person outside the family signs in with.
- Satisfies: none given. Cited: LEGAL-REQ-006 (P0, `docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md:63-67`).
- Problem and evidence (reproduced on an unmodified copy of `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/machine.logic.ts` at e4fd94d (the file is the same at 2980f3e), run in Node with `--experimental-strip-types`; not run on a phone):
  1. `CONSENT_RECORDED` works out the sync mode from the answered step alone: `const sync: SyncMode = event.step === 'sensitive' && !event.accepted ? 'off' : 'on';` (`machine.logic.ts:171`). It forgets an earlier decline when only Terms or the age line is asked again.
  2. The sequence: `GATE_LOADED` with Terms current, age attested and `sensitiveDeclined: true` gives `ready`, `sync: 'off'`. A later read with Terms no longer current and `sensitiveDeclined: true` gives `needsConsent`, steps `['terms']` (`consentSteps`, `:94-100`). `CONSENT_RECORDED` with Terms accepted then gives `ready`, `sync: 'on'`.
  3. Until the next gate read (a foreground more than 30 minutes after the last, `session-provider.tsx:113`, `:246`; `shouldRecheckGate` is false for `sync: 'on'` before that, `machine.logic.ts:236-237`; the provider does not read again after recording, `:466`), the Privacy row (`sensitive-row.ts:41-44`) and the Account row both read On for a declined consent, `canSync` is true (`machine.logic.ts:225-226`), `syncAllowed()` is true (`auth-store.ts:84-86`, `:98-100`) and the sync engine can start (`sync/index.ts:186`). I expect the server's consent gate to hold the pushes: `sync_push` returns `paused` on `SCCON` (`supabase/migrations/20261016000000_sync_v1_server.sql:1265-1267`), which `public.require_content_consent()` raises unless Terms, age and sensitive-data consent all stand (`supabase/migrations/20261003000000_security_and_family.sql:189-206`), and the withdrawn case on real SQL ends in `paused_consent` (`apps/mobile/test/sync-e2e.test.ts:424-441`). Whether a declined sensitive-data consent from this reducer sequence behaves the same was not run by me: unverified. If it does, the engine sits in `paused_consent`, a phase that never reaches the Privacy row (BL-502 point 5), so the row reads On while nothing uploads.
- Scope: the reducer must not turn sync on unless the last gate allowed content. The owner picks and says why: carry what the gate said into `needsConsent` (for example `sensitiveDeclined`), or read the gate again after recording.
- Done when: a failing reducer test first, in `apps/mobile/test/auth-machine.test.ts`, with the sequence above and the same sequence for the age step; then the fix, with the existing cases still green (a decline answered in the same pass still gives `off`, and a pass where every step is accepted gives `on`).

#### BL-504 useSensitiveDataStatus returns the `open` it read at render, so a mounted row can keep a stale one

- Scope: keep `{ status, open }` together in state and set both in `attach` (`privacy-sources.ts:55-59`), or bump a version in `attach`; the owner picks.
- Done when: a hook test with the stand-in (`apps/mobile/test/helpers/mini-react.ts`, used by `privacy-sensitive-row.test.ts`) mounts the hook with a source that has no `open`, registers one that has an `open` and the same status, and sees the new `open`; it fails on the current hook.

#### BL-508 The test that the session provider registers the Privacy row is a formatting-sensitive regex
- Status: done (PR #1252, 909535447: the effect moved into `useRegisterSensitiveDataRow`, and `apps/mobile/test/privacy-sensitive-row.test.ts` mounts it and checks the row follows the auth snapshot). Mode: agent. Owner: qa engineer, mobile engineer. Milestone: M5. Size: S. Depends on: none.

- Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given.
- Problem and evidence (re-opened on `develop` at e4fd94d): `apps/mobile/test/privacy-sensitive-row.test.ts:256-258` pins the provider with two regexes on its comment-stripped text, an import line and `useEffect(() => { registerSensitiveDataRow(); }, [])`. The effect is at `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/session-provider.tsx:193-195`. A harmless reformat (another callback shape, the effect moved into a hook) turns the test red while the behaviour holds, and a registration moved somewhere that never runs would still pass. The provider imports React Native and cannot render in Node, and the repo has no component renderer (the header of `apps/mobile/test/helpers/mini-react.ts`: no `react-test-renderer`, tests run in a Node environment); the stand-in covers hooks only.
- Scope: if the effect can move into a small hook in a file the stand-in can run, replace the regexes with a behavioural check that mounting it registers a source whose `read` follows the auth snapshot. If not, keep the regexes, add a comment on them saying what they pin and what a refactor must keep, and record that here.
- Done when: either a test fails when the registration call is removed from what runs on mount, or the pin carries its reason and this entry says it is left as it is.
- Outcome: the effect moved into `useRegisterSensitiveDataRow` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/sensitive-row-hook.ts`, no React Native); the test mounts it on the hook stand-in and checks the row follows the auth snapshot, and the provider pin now only needs the hook call in its body, whatever the formatting. Mutants: removing the registration fails the behaviour test; dropping the provider call fails the pin; a reformat of either passes.

#### BL-775 A failed Erase everything that the person keeps using erases only what existed when it began
- Status: ready (BL-387 is done in code). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M-JR. Size: S. Severity: S1. Area: front. Why S1: it can lose a word, which the legend puts at S0, but the failed line warns the person first, it needs a failed erase that the person chose to start, and CCO-6 rules it not blocking.
- Satisfies: DATA-REQ-024 (Erase everything on a phone that never signed in); DATA-REQ-014 and F17-REQ-080 (the Delete this book half of BL-387, same wipe path). Also cited: D-144, CCO-6. No requirement yet says that a retry spares what is written after a failed erase; the Requirement line below is that rule (CCO-6 rules the gap not blocking, and the CPO's 9 Nov council answer, which is outside the repository and in no executive-log entry, lists it among the things to build next). Who must rule: nobody before the work starts; the founder approves any new failed-line words before they merge (D-144).
- Who: `mobile`; review `privacy`, `data-steward`.
- Problem: PR #520, which is BL-387's work, is merged. In #520, `eraseEverythingLocal` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/store.ts:1030`) writes the pending mark `erase.everything.pending` (a time) and, when a recording file will not go, returns `incomplete` with the rows and the mark still there. The person can then keep using the app. The next launch (`resumeEraseAtLaunch`, `apps/mobile/src/lib/erase-everything.ts:124`) and a retry from the screen both call `eraseEverythingLocal` again, which removes every row then present, so a letter written after the failure goes too. The failed line tells the person so (it ends "and that erases anything you add before then", D-144), so the screen is true, but new words are lost with no way back. `apps/mobile/test/erase-all.test.ts:588` pins today's behaviour. CCO-6 lists it as open and not blocking.
- Requirement: a retry and the launch resume erase only what existed when the mark was written. What the person writes after the mark is kept, and the PR says how it tells old from new for each table and for the files.
- Acceptance:
  - Given an Erase everything that ended `incomplete` because one recording would not go, and a new letter kept after it, when the file can be removed and the erase runs again (a retry, or the next launch), then every row and file that existed when the mark was written is gone and the new letter and its recording are still there.
  - Given a kill part way through an erase and nothing written afterwards, when the app next opens, then the store is empty and the 18+ question shows, as today.
  - Given the new behaviour, when the content tests run, then `copy.settings.erase.failed` no longer says that anything added is erased, and the founder has approved the new wording (D-144: a change to these lines goes back to him).
- Tests: change the case at `erase-all.test.ts:588` and add the two above, each failing on the old code.
- Extends: PR #520, BL-387, CCO-6, D-144.

#### BL-778 Delete or document the build-time override LEGAL_CONTENT_DIR before the 0.9.0 pages are deployed
- Status: done in code (#710, ae15e212; `git grep -n LEGAL_CONTENT_DIR -- apps .github` finds nothing at d4b8f5f1; the post-deploy sha256 check of CR-60 stays the gate). Mode: pair. Owner: platform. Milestone: M9. Size: XS. Severity: S1. Area: web.
- Satisfies: LEGAL-REQ-001 (the versioned page a person agrees to serves the version recorded). Also cited: BL-565, CR-60. Who must rule: nobody; #710 made the change. #710's guard test over the three files that read the texts is a tripwire, not a proof.
- Who: the web lane (the website thread, outside the roster) makes the change; the Mode is `pair` so the dispatcher does not take it (`docs/agents/HARNESS.md` section 6: it never assigns the website thread's tasks); the owner name is `platform` (`ops`) because the row gates the deploy of the 0.9.0 pages; review `security`.
- Problem (as found on 8 Nov 2026, before #710): `apps/web/src/lib/legal/documents.ts:49` reads `process.env.LEGAL_CONTENT_DIR` before the committed folder `apps/web/content/legal`. In code, `git grep LEGAL_CONTENT_DIR -- apps .github` on 8 Nov 2026 finds only that line; the only other mention is CR-60. The 0.9.0 pages and raw `.md` files are pinned by sha256 in `packages/content/test/legal-beta.test.ts` and `apps/web/test/legal-served.test.ts`, which run in CI where nothing sets the variable. The web build (`next build`, `apps/web/vercel.json`) checks no hash. If the variable were set in the hosting project only, the live pages could serve other bytes than the ones pinned. No test or build step would catch that; the post-deploy `curl | sha256sum` check (#616 step 6, CR-60) would.
- Requirement: delete the override, or keep it, document in `documents.ts` and in `docs/ops` what sets it, who may and that the production project must not, and pin that with a test. CR-60 puts this before the first deploy of the 0.9.0 pages.
- Acceptance:
  - Given the repository, when `git grep LEGAL_CONTENT_DIR -- apps .github` runs, then it finds nothing (the override is deleted), or finds only `documents.ts` with its comment and the test below, and `docs/ops` says the production project does not set it.
  - Given the override kept, when the variable points at a folder whose bytes differ from the pinned ones, then a test in `apps/web/test` fails.
  - Given the override deleted, when the web tests run, then the pins still pass and the pages read the committed folder only.
- Extends: CR-60, BL-565, PR #652.

- Status: needs-founder (the first rehearsal of the runbook, which the founder walks alone; the runbook itself is done, #711, d4b8f5f1; the emailed account deletion, Route 1, waits for BL-551). Mode: human. Owner: platform. Milestone: M9. Size: XS. Severity: S1. Area: ops.

Runbooks exist for closing an under-18 account (`docs/ops/runbooks/underage-account.md`) and for a deletion that did not finish (`stuck-deletion.md`). The request matrix in `docs/engineering/08-data-rights-and-legal-requests.md` already lists the routes: delete account by email (verify by a link to the account address), export/access and correction by email (correction by profile fields only, "through a runbook"), and withdraw consent (`record_policy_act`, method `support_assisted`). - Acceptance (the runbook's text is read at d4b8f5f1 to cover the four cases, not walked; the rehearsal checks them):

  - Given an email asking to see, export or correct, when the runbook is followed, then it ends with what the person receives or what changed, and the same check came first.

- Extends: BL-551, BL-237, BL-565, CR-60, the request matrix in chapter 08, DSR-R02, DSR-R05, `underage-account.md`, `stuck-deletion.md`.

### Follow-up from the 9 Nov 2026 Write autosave fix (#725)

#### BL-816 Review's typed-text writer has no maximum wait, so a crash in a long burst of editing loses more than the last 300 ms
- Status: done in code (#750, fc7c0afb, merged 10 Nov 2026). It has not run on a phone. It is in the build uploaded to App Store Connect by `testflight.yml` run 42791080592 on develop 5433323c (profile testflight, EAS build number 12, 1.0.0 (12), started 10 Nov 2026 at 1:29 AM PST, upload logged at 1:48 AM PST); I did not see Apple finish processing it, and did not check whether it reached testers. The EAS build counter ran 10, 11, 12 across those three runs with no gap, so I found no sign of a build cut by hand, but I did not check App Store Connect. His words were "Ok continue with your recommendation", in answer to a list whose item on this row read "BL-816 severity: I recommend S1. S0 would hold the next alpha."; he did not name BL-816 or the C0 to C1 step. Under `docs/ops/RELEASE.md` 5.4 and TF-09 as quoted below, an S1 does not hold the C0 to C1 step; that is Karma's reading of those documents, not something he said. No D- entry has been made. Moving this row to done in code does not clear it: Karma's reading is that it stays an open S1 for the submission step until S1-166 has been walked and passed on a build that has the fix (1.0.0 (12) or later), and the founder has not ruled on when it closes. The gates that say no open S0 or S1 (TF-09, B2-18, RT-REL-12) read an issue list with labels; the repo has no `S0` or `S1` label yet (BL-005, FT-20; checked 10 Nov 2026) and no GitHub issue names BL-816, so a gate check run from the issue list will not see this row. S1-166 in `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md` has not been run (as of 10 Nov 2026) and the phone check stays open until it is walked; what a write every 300 ms costs on the SE 3 is judged there by feel, in (d), and was measured only in Node (about 0.5 ms median). Differences from this row, as built: the bound is 300 ms, chosen for its margin under the 500 ms ceiling and not from a phone measurement; the writer has one timer, not the two the Requirement words, and Review B of #750 accepted that, finding that its writes match a two-timer writer's unless a write throws, and then the words wait for the next change or flush instead of one retry on a timer; RT-REV-02 and RT-REV-07 are `partial`, not `gap`, because a Node case and a written device step now exist (Review B of #750 accepted that too); the new cases are in `review-writer-autosave.test.ts` (24 cases, 9 of which fail on the old logic and 15 of which pin behaviour that must not change), not in `store.review-v9.test.ts`; S1-166 (c) checks the recording only and the original words are checked in Node. Still open: the PRD rewording (Problem item 7, the CPO's) and BL-377's stale status. Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M-JR. Size: S. Severity: S1 (accepted by the founder on 9 Nov 2026; see Status). Area: front. The legend of the 1 Nov audit section puts anything that can lose a word at S0, and F06-REQ-036 is P0 with the acceptance "100 of 100 kills reopen with the same text", which a burst of editing in Review broke before #750. S0 versus S1 is a release gate: `docs/ops/RELEASE.md` 5.4 and TF-09 let a cohort go from C0 to C1 only with no open S0, and let the submission step go only with no open S0 or S1. So the call is release scope, which is the founder's. Karma recommended S1 on 9 Nov 2026 and the founder accepted S1 (see Status). The reasons are Karma's, and the founder did not see them in the list he answered: S1 for the next TestFlight build, because the loss needs a crash, a kill or a power loss inside an unbroken burst (a pause of 300 ms or more flushes, which ordinary typing usually has; not measured), every graceful exit flushes first, and only that session's edits on top of saved words are at risk; Karma's plan is to have it fixed before the 1 Dec submission. Unlike BL-775, no CCO-6 ruling calls this not blocking, and the loss is silent: nothing on screen warns the person.
- Satisfies: F06-REQ-036 (P0: Review never loses work; any change in Review is written to the draft within 500 ms, and 100 of 100 kills in Review reopen with the same text; also `docs/prd/v2/06-nfr.md:190`), which was not met in a burst before #750; F04-REQ-011 and RT-WRT-05 (typed text: at most the last 500 ms of typing lost; the requirement's home is Write, and Change words in Review is typed text too). Before #750 (read on 9 Nov 2026; #750 made RT-REV-02 and RT-REV-07 `partial` and pointed them at its test and S1-166), no release-catalog row named Review's writer or a bound on typed words lost in Review: RT-WRT-05 names `write-autosave.test.ts` and S1-36, both Write's; RT-REV-02 (edits put back survive a kill, SR-C-06) and RT-REV-07 (kills in Review keep text, kind, date and child) were both `gap` at `scripts/qa/release-catalog.rows.mjs:94` and `:99`, and the catalog listed no evidence at all for RT-REV-07, though the replay test's header names both. Who must rule: the founder accepted S1 on 9 Nov 2026 (see Status); the bound is the mobile owner's call (below); the PRD rewording (Problem item 7) is the CPO's proposal to take up.
- Who: `mobile`; review `qa`, `privacy`. Dispatch: the dispatcher takes the first eligible task in file order with no severity ordering (`scripts/agents/dispatch.mjs:332`), and on 9 Nov 2026 BL-816 was position 46 of 46 in the `mobile` queue (the first is BL-355). If it must land before outside testers, Karma assigns it to a mobile session directly or the row moves up the file; Mode stays agent. Done means done in code: the row is done in code when the fix and its tests merge, and the phone check stays open until the Review device step below is walked.
- Problem: read in code on `develop` at c350be3e (9 Nov 2026), not run on a phone.
  1. `reviewWriter().text()` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/capture/review-persist.logic.ts` (lines 188-192) sets `pending`, stops the timer and starts a new one for `TYPED_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` (300 ms, line 25) on every call. It is a pure debounce with no maximum wait, the shape Write's autosave had before #725 (e5cc7ecd; `docs/design/screens/WRITE.md` section 11 item 7). A burst of editing with no gap of 300 ms writes nothing until the burst ends, so a kill in the middle loses all of it, not "at most the keystrokes of the last 300 ms" as the comment above the constant (lines 20-24) says; that holds only after a pause.
  2. Review's edits of the person's words do go through it: the Change words field (`review.tsx:981`, `onChangeText={setUserText}`) reaches `writer.text(userText)` (`:321-325`), whose callback is `setDraftReview` (`:306-308`), which writes `drafts.review_text` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/db/repos/drafts.ts:261-286`). That is the only autosave of those words. The write is silent: Review shows no autosave line, makes no announcement and does not render for it. It never touches the recording, `raw_transcript` or `typed_text`.
  3. The 300 ms is the quiet window the file puts under F04-REQ-011's 500 ms. #522 (34f848b7) added it; no reason for 300 rather than 500 is recorded. Each write is a synchronous SQLite write while the person types, and Write's is 500 ms.
  4. The flush paths, all of which write the newest words first: the app leaving the foreground (`inactive` or `background`, `review.tsx:311-313`), the screen unmounting (`:314-317`), Done (`:327-329`), Close (`:886-889`) and Keep (`:539`); `review-persist.wiring.test.ts` pins them. So the exposure is a crash, an OS kill of the foreground app, a flat battery or a force restart in the middle of a burst, the same as Write's, and not the app switcher or leaving the app. `review.tsx` never calls `cancel`; only `store.review-v9.test.ts:188` does.
  5. The replay test (`apps/mobile/test/review-persist.replay.test.ts`) models the debounce: its `durableText` moves only after 300 ms of quiet, so it counts a whole burst as lost and passes today. A writer with a maximum wait fails it at seed 40, so the model must change with the fix. The catalog lists no evidence for RT-REV-07 although this test's header names RT-REV-02 and RT-REV-07; the fix updates both rows.
  6. A second defect in the same function, the retry. `flush` clears `pending` before it writes, and `safe` swallows a throw, so a write that throws is retried only by a later change; the comment in `safe` says Done and Close retry it too, and they do not, because `flush` then finds nothing pending. `setDraftReview` returns false for a draft in `recording` or `discarding`, a missing draft or an empty base (`drafts.ts:261-286`); that is a refusal, not a failure, and the writer neither sees it nor should retry it.
  7. F04-REQ-011 (`docs/prd/v2/features/F04-capture.md:319`) and `docs/prd/v2/06-nfr.md:59` still say "written 500 ms after the last keystroke", which is the debounce #725 fixed in Write. The bound that holds is the second sentence of F04-REQ-011 and `06-nfr.md:189`: at most the last 500 ms of typing lost. A rewording to "written at least every 500 ms while typing" is a proposal for the CPO; `docs/prd` is not edited by this row or its PR.
  8. Two comments are stale and are corrected with the change: the header of `review-persist.logic.ts` (line 14) cites `test/review-persist.test.ts`, which does not exist, and the comment above the constant (item 1).
- Requirement: at most the last `TYPED_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` of editing in Review is lost on a kill, however long the burst. The number is the owner's call: 300 ms (today's) or up to 500 ms both meet the P0 ceiling of 500 ms (F04-REQ-011, F06-REQ-036); the owner states in the PR what a write costs on the phone they measured and prefers 500, as Write does, unless 300 is justified by it. As #725 did for Write: the first change after a write arms a write timer that later changes do not move, and when it fires it writes the newest words, not the words it was armed with; the quiet-window timer stays, so a real pause is still found where it is. With two timers, `cancel` clears both and `flush` leaves none. Nothing visible changes: the mid-burst write goes through the same silent callback, so Review gains no status line, announcement or render; if the owner adds any "saved" line or announcement to Review, it comes only after a real pause, as in #725 (`persist(value, quiet)` and `settled`, `write-session.logic.ts`). Words a mid-burst write already took are not written twice. Retry: a write that throws leaves the words pending, and they are tried again at the next change, at Done, at Close and at the unmount, and only there: no timer re-arms itself after a failure, so a draft that is gone cannot loop. A false return is a refusal and is not retried. The words written, `base` and `drafts.review_*` are unchanged; raw_transcript and typed_text are never read for writing.
- Acceptance (labelled by defect, so a reviewer can reject one half):
  - Maximum wait. Given Review on Asha's letter and Change words typing, one change every 100 ms for 3 s with no pause, when everything in memory is dropped at any moment (the kill model of `review-persist.replay.test.ts`, fake timers, the real writer and store), then the draft holds the newest words but at most `TYPED_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` of typing, and the reopened Review (`mountReview`) shows them. This fails on the old logic, which writes nothing during the burst.
  - Maximum wait. Given the same burst running for 30 s, then writes keep coming at the same interval, each holding the newest words and not the words that armed the timer.
  - Maximum wait. Given one change and then a pause, then one write at the bound and no second write; given a burst and then a pause, then the newest words are written once.
  - Maximum wait. Given a burst, when Done, Close, the app leaving the foreground or Keep calls `flush`, then the newest words are written once and no timer is left; given a burst, when `cancel` is called, then nothing is written afterwards (a case beside `store.review-v9.test.ts:188`; the screen does not call `cancel` today).
  - Maximum wait. Given a burst, then nothing reaches the screen: the callback in `review.tsx` only calls `setDraftReview` (source pin, as #725's quiet test).
  - Maximum wait. Given the 100 seeded runs of the replay test with its model changed to the new bound (words durable within the window after the first unwritten change, not after quiet), then all 100 reopen with all but at most the last `TYPED_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` of typing.
  - Retry after a throw. Given a write that throws in the middle of a burst, then the words stay pending and the next change, Done, Close and the unmount write them again; nothing is retried on a timer after the throw.
  - Retry after a throw. Given a write that is refused (the callback returns false or the draft is gone), then it is not retried and nothing reaches the screen.
  - Device: Review has no hard-stop step. S1-36 (m) is Write's (type for about 10 s with no gap of half a second, force restart with Volume Up, Volume Down and the side button, never the app switcher, then compare the draft). Add a Review equivalent with an unused S1 id (`git grep` the id on `develop` and in open PRs first): open Review on a letter, tap Change words, type with no gap of 300 ms for about 10 s, force restart as in (m), reopen the draft from Tonight, and expect all but about the last second of the edit, with the recording and the original words intact. Point RT-REV-02 and RT-REV-07 (`scripts/qa/release-catalog.rows.mjs` and `docs/qa/release-test-catalog.csv`) at the new test and step, as #725 did for RT-WRT-05; they stay `gap` until the step is walked.
- Tests: new cases in `apps/mobile/test/store.review-v9.test.ts` beside the `[F04-REQ-011]` block, titles naming F06-REQ-036 and F04-REQ-011; the replay model in `review-persist.replay.test.ts` changed; each new case fails with only the source change reverted.
- Extends: #725 (e5cc7ecd), #522 (34f848b7), F06-REQ-036, F04-REQ-011, RT-WRT-05, RT-REV-02, RT-REV-07; and BL-377, which still reads ready with Depends on BL-148 although #522 cites it, so its status is stale (not changed here; this row does not close it).

#### BL-922 Hold a needsConsent session with no local book out of the child step; one account read on the consent sheet
- Status: partly done (PR #1126 is part 1; part 2 is open PR #1167). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M15 (after build 13; Karma places it). Size: M. Depends on: #764.
- Satisfies: NX-36-S17 (Tier 0: the child step is never shown while the account's book may be on its way). Also cited: NX-31-R12 (the claim screen, #737), CR-61.
- Problem: read in code at 6c5e5f31 (#764), not run on a phone. `heldNewPhoneView` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/first-run/gate.logic.ts`) holds `checkingConsent`, `ready` with sync `unknown` and `signingOut` with sync on or unknown, and leaves `needsConsent` to the earlier route, so a returning account with no local book whose consent is outstanding (a kill on the Terms sheet and a relaunch, or a Terms version bumped since its last acceptance; `my_sync_gate()` is per account) sees the promise step with Continue and no consent sheet: the sheet is pushed only from the sign-in screens and Settings > Account > Finish setup (`app/settings/account.tsx:227`), and nothing pushes it at relaunch. No pull can reach that session (canSync is false, the engine is stopped), so nothing lands. A book made there has no owner (`takeOwnership` in `lib/sync/ownership.ts` runs only from `onSignedIn`), so when Finish setup completes consent the claim screen shows before anything moves (`accountClaimPending()` in `lib/auth/auth-store.ts`, `consentHandoff` answering `askClaim` in `lib/first-run/handoff.logic.ts`, the claim step of `app/(auth)/sign-in/consent.tsx`; #737): "Keep your letters in this account?" with the second-book body, Keep in this account and Not my account. The second book follows Keep; Not my account ends the session with the phone as it was. Recovery in build 13 is Hide this book on the extra book until F17-REQ-026 (server-side book deletion) ships: Delete this book is refused once the owner is written (`lib/store.ts` `localDeletionAllowed`; the row is hidden in `app/settings/children/[id].tsx`), and the staging operator removes the extra book on request. No letter is lost. Lens B M3 and lens A note 2 at 6c5e5f31, corrected by lens A item 3 and lens B M4 at d38e8b69; accepted for build 13 by CR-61 (amended 17 Nov), which names this row as the way back.
- Scope: (1) hold a `needsConsent` session with no local book out of the child step: push the consent sheet again at relaunch, or show a held screen with its own words and a way forward within 10 seconds (Finish setup and Try another way; never a dead end for App Review); (2) lens A should-fix 3 at 5e896fed: the consent sheet's own `readAccountBooks` (`app/(auth)/sign-in/consent.tsx:134`, the `noBook` branch at :193) duplicates the route's ask (`lib/first-run/use-new-phone.ts`), so a returning account with no book can meet No book here yet twice and tap Start a book twice; keep one reader and one screen, and rewrite the #737 pins in `apps/mobile/test/first-run-new-account.test.ts` (:152-156, two `readAccountBooks(` calls) with it. Not in scope: the claim screen at Finish setup, which #737 built and which shows today (read at d38e8b69). Any new words are the founder's (NX-36 S5, S7) and land through `packages/content` with the content rules test; none ships without them.
- Done when: a `needsConsent` session with no local book never answers `childStep` (pinned beside the hold cases in `apps/mobile/test/new-phone-route.test.ts` and `apps/mobile/test/use-first-run-route.test.ts`, red on the old code); `sync_books` is read once per launch for a returning account with no book; `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md` S1-204 (k) is rewritten to expect the sheet or the held screen, not the promise step; the "Known gap" clause at `gate.logic.ts` heldNewPhoneView and the pointers to it in `use-first-run-route.ts` are removed in the same PR.

#### BL-859 The moment engine: a pure function from {day, cityKey} to moments with reason codes (NX-39-R15, R5)
- Status: blocked (Memory Library is parked until after the first photo release, plan 17). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M15. Size: M.

No import of network, clock, locale, randomness or storage; an import-graph test. Day bucket is the phone's zone, passed in: `dayKeyAt(epochMs, utcOffsetMinutes)` stays in `moments.ts` as a pure helper (the caller supplies the offset). Reason codes and `cityKey` null for a moment with two or more cities are as defined in R15. Tests: determinism over 100 shuffles, order invariance, idempotence, monotonicity in the limited form of R15 (adding no-city items or a city the day already has never uncovers a day; a different city between matching days may split a moment), midnight, DST, flight day, empty, null place, one huge day; fictional family "Asha". Not wired to any screen.
- Fails on old code: `[NX-39-R15] the same {day, cityKey} list always makes the same moments, with reason codes and no forbidden import`.

#### BL-861 The consent state machine: layers, states and acts, never at launch (NX-39-R3, R47, R48)
- Status: blocked (Memory Library is parked until after the first photo release, plan 17). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M15. Size: M.
- Who: `mobile`, `privacy`.
- Satisfies: NX-39-R3, NX-39-R47, NX-39-R48. Also cited: PRIV-R21, CDESO-1, CPO-15.
- Scope: a pure state machine for `media_read`, `media_background` and `occasions`: Not asked, Held, All, Limited, Denied, Narrowed, Revoked; the only caller of an authorization request is the Continue event; Not now holds and never returns from a note; no switch on without its act; an adapter interface for the PRIV-R21 act writer (its location and act vocabulary are UNVERIFIED and counsel-adjacent; do not guess them). Acts are `agreed` and `withdrawn` only: "Not now", a cancel and a system revoke record none. After "Not now", a chooser tap shows no sheet and the picker keeps working; only opening the control does. Narrowed records no new act, wipes the index and leaves one plain ledger note (counsel question CB-28). `media_background` and `occasions` follow the state tables in NX-39 section 7.3.1 (the seven states, with Limited and Narrowed only for `media_read`). Tests drive every launch path (cold, warm, notification tap, deep link, first run) and assert 0 requests.
- Fails on old code: `[NX-39-R3] no launch path requests photo authorization and Not now holds`.
- Done when: that title and `[NX-39-R47] each consent layer records its own act and no switch is on without it` pass against a fake writer.
- Plan: P2a, P2b, P2c, P4a; install yes; no founder hours.

- Problem: `store.ts` marks a draft `discarding` and then removes it (around lines 1267 and 1290). If the app stops between the two steps, or the file delete fails (#824), the draft stays `discarding`: hidden, with its audio still on the phone. `apps/mobile/src/lib/capture/sweep.logic.ts` and `sweep.ts` do not mention `discarding` at all, though comments in `store.ts`, `let-it-go.logic.ts` and `sync/merge.ts` say a launch sweep finishes it.

## Locked pack: the rest of the work (20 Nov 2026)

Written 20 Nov 2026 by Karma with the CPO role, docs only, after the requirements were locked (founder, 19 Nov: "I approve all requirements."; record `docs/product/prd/16-council-review-round-2.md`). Every row cites the card rows it satisfies; the card is the source of truth and wins where a row and a card differ. BL-950 and BL-951 are the engineering thread's (#832 follow-ups and NS-01-R17 iCloud progress); this section starts at BL-952. Facts were read on develop `4f89d659` and the open photo and Find stacks; nothing was run on a phone. No row turns a flag on in `production`. Device rows follow ruling D13 (a test install holding only the Asha book). Words marked PROPOSED need the founder's approval before any build outside his family shows them.

How the harness reads this section: a row is eligible when its Status is `ready`, or `blocked` on backlog ids that are all done, and every `Depends on` id is done (`scripts/agents/lib.mjs`). A row blocked on a counsel answer, a founder step or an unmerged PR names it in words, so the dispatcher leaves it alone until a person changes the status.

## First-run build steps, instrumentation and the P0 rows the groups missed (21 Nov 2026, proposed)

Written 21 Nov 2026 by the product agent, docs only. The readiness check (`docs/product/READINESS-20nov.md`, PR #1079) found work in the dependency map that has no BL id: the 21 first-run PRs of `docs/tdd/new-scope/12-first-run-5.md` (FP-1 to FP-20, FP-11 unused), three data rows and two native-security rows beside them, the perf profile half of BL-929, and 100 instrumentation rows. They get ids BL-1021 to BL-1149 below, one row each, in the order the map lists them, so the map id (FP-n, DA-n, NSC-n, IN-...) is named in every title and a reader can go from the map to the row and back. BL-1048 and BL-1049 are two P0 rows no group row names (NS-08-R21 and FR-MKT-44, both added by errata after the groups were written).

Every row is `proposed`: the dispatcher skips it until Karma or the founder sets `ready`. Dependencies are the map's, translated to BL ids; a wait on something that has no BL row is written in Scope. Mode is `pair` where the map names a founder, counsel, device or account step, `agent` where it names none. Nothing here copies or changes a requirement. ## Review follow-ups from 20 to 21 Nov 2026 (proposed)

Written 21 Nov 2026 by the product agent, docs only. Every row is `proposed`: Karma or the founder sets it to `ready`, and the priorities here are the product agent's proposal, not an approval. The first row is a hard blocker for turning the backup flag on. Sources are review comments and PR bodies, linked in each row.

#### BL-1150 Backup is iOS only: a platform gate before the flag can turn on (B5)
- Status: proposed (Lens B review on PR #1112, https://github.com/thesaurabhpareek/earlyletters/pull/1112; Karma or the founder sets it to ready). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer, security engineer (security lens required). Milestone: M15. Size: S.
- Satisfies: BRIEF B5, CR-71 B5.
- Blocks: setting `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKUP` on (and so every backup flag step, BL-1151 and BL-1198).
- Problem: HARD BLOCKER for setting `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKUP` on. `apps/mobile/src/lib/capabilities.ts` gates backup on the build flag alone. On Android and in Expo Go `ScribeFiles` is null, so the exclusion read-back is always false: the state file is deleted at each launch and the store always refuses to open it.
- Scope: one platform check in `lib/capabilities.ts` so backup is available only on iOS with the native file module present; the launch call in `lib/backup/gate.ts` and the store open in `runtime.ts` skip quietly when it is off. A test per case: iOS with the module, iOS without it, Android, Expo Go (flag on in each), none of them deletes or refuses anything.
- Done when: with the flag on, Android and Expo Go never delete the state file and never refuse to open; iOS behaves as before; the security lens has read the diff.

#### BL-1151 Backup launch result is shown and late sidecar files are re-checked (B5)
- Status: proposed (PR #1112 body, "Known limits" and Karma's note, https://github.com/thesaurabhpareek/earlyletters/pull/1112; Karma or the founder sets it to ready). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer, privacy engineer. Milestone: M15. Size: S. Depends on: BL-1150.
- Satisfies: BRIEF B5, CR-71 B5.
- Problem: `startBackup` returns the failed-delete count (`failed`) and the list-failed count (`listFailed`), and `safely(startBackup)` in `apps/mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx` drops both. Separately, an SQLite `-wal` or `-shm` file created later in the same session stays unexcluded from the phone backup until the next launch.
- Scope: (a) carry both counts out of `safely` to a content-free local record (counts only, no file names that carry a profile id) that a reviewer or the support export can read, with a test that a non-zero count is kept. (b) Decide and build one mitigation for late sidecar files: re-check after the first write of the session, or when the app goes to the background. Write the decision and the reason in the PR body.
- Done when: the counts reach a place a person can read before the flag is on; the late-file case has a test showing the sidecar is excluded within the same session or at background; the privacy lens has read the diff.

#### BL-1404 The .env guard prints a line with no "=" whole into the FAIL message, so a secret could reach the console and CI logs
- Status: done (PR #1457 merged as `6045c5403`). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer, security engineer. Milestone: M12. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Satisfies: none given. Cited: CLAUDE.md privacy rules (no secret in a log); Review B on #1219 (finding 2); BL-506 (the guard and its test).
- Problem (read in `apps/mobile/scripts/env-file-guard.mjs` lines 32 to 36): `envFileProblems` does `line.split('=')` and pushes `${file}: ${k}`, where `k` is everything before the first `=`. A line with no `=` (a bare `sb_secret_...`) or one that uses `:` (`SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: sb_secret_...`) is therefore echoed whole. Review B on #1219 confirmed it by calling the guard; the pin is the `it.fails` "a line with no "=" does not put its text into the FAIL message" in `apps/mobile/test/preflight-planted-env.test.ts`. PR #1219 is merged (`c52582bf`), so the pin is on develop.
- Scope: the FAIL message never echoes any content from a line, only the file name and a line number. Print a variable name only when the line contains `=` and the text before the first `=` is a variable name (letters, digits, underscore, starting with a letter or underscore); for every other line (no `=`, a `:` separator, spaces, anything else) print `<file>: <unparsable line N>` with the line number and nothing from the line. A bare token such as `sb_secret_...` matches the name pattern but has no `=`, so it is never printed. Same change flips the `it.fails` to a plain `it`.
- Done when: the pin is a plain `it` and passes; one new case in `envFileProblems`' string tests covers a no-`=` secret line (a bare `sb_secret_...`), a line containing `:` (`KEY: value`) and a line with spaces, and for each the output holds the line number and file name and none of the line's text; one more case checks that a `KEY=value` line still names the key and never the value; the existing 12 tests in the planted-env file still pass.
- Test: `apps/mobile/test/preflight-planted-env.test.ts` (pin flipped), `apps/mobile/test/account-deletion-switch.test.ts` (string cases for `envFileProblems`).
- Gate: none. The pin goes red as an unexpected pass if the guard is fixed and the pin is not flipped, so both land in one PR.

#### BL-1420 Each new claim is its own file, so adding a claim never conflicts with another PR
- Status: proposed (Karma ruled option A on #1265; product sets `ready` after #1265 merges). Mode: agent. Owner: platform. Milestone: M15. Size: M. Depends on: none.
- Satisfies: none given. Cited: `docs/agents/COORDINATION.md` section 2 and 3 (claims; the 17 Oct note that a shared last line made every pair of PRs conflict); HV2-007 as named in `scripts/agents/board-check.mjs`.
- Problem: every PR adds its row to the same table in `docs/agents/CLAIMS.md`, so each merge conflicts the next. Evidence read in the PR threads on 21 Nov: PR #1219 merged develop into itself twice for a one-hunk `CLAIMS.md` conflict (heads `01a7c99c`, then `d5d509a5`), and PR #1216 once (`7271977d`), each time "both sides added a row at the same spot in the table". A PR also deletes its own row when it merges, which is a second place two PRs can collide.
- Ruling (Karma, comment on #1265): option A, one file per claim, is the chosen design; option B is not taken, because `merge=union` hides real conflicts. The way back is to restore the single table from git. The change touches `scripts/agents/**` and `docs/agents/**`, so it needs two counted reviews, a fresh builder agent, and the harness owner checks that `check.mjs` and the merge queue still read claims.
- Option A (ruled): one file per claim, `docs/agents/claims/<id>.md`, holding the same columns as front matter (owner session, branch, PR, globs, claimed, expires, note). A new claim is a new file and a finished one is a deleted file, so two PRs only conflict when they claim the same id, which is the real collision. `scripts/agents/board-check.mjs` reads the folder and enforces the 15-row limit by file count; `docs/agents/CLAIMS.md` becomes a short rules page with no table.
- Option B (not taken): keep the table and add `docs/agents/CLAIMS.md merge=union` in `.gitattributes`. Cheaper, but a union merge keeps both sides of a deleted row, so a finished claim can come back silently; not recommended.
- Scope (option A, as ruled): the folder and a first-run migration of the live rows (10 on 21 Nov); the parser in `scripts/agents/board-check.mjs` and its test (the live-file test at `board-check.test.mjs:119` reads `CLAIMS.md` today); every other reader found by search: `scripts/agents/merge-queue.mjs`, `scripts/agents/brief.mjs`, `scripts/status/today.mjs`; the wording in `docs/agents/COORDINATION.md` sections 2 and 3, `docs/agents/OPERATING_MODEL.md`, `docs/agents/HARNESS.md` and the lane prompts under `docs/agents/lanes/`. Several of these may not need a change; the owner checks each. Per-agent charters that name the file (`.claude/agents/`, `agents/*/MEMORY.md`) are updated in a second PR if the first would pass CODE-R02.
- Done when: two scratch PRs that each add a different claim merge in either order with no conflict; `node scripts/agents/board-check.mjs` and `node --test 'scripts/agents/*.test.mjs'` pass on the folder; the old table is gone from `CLAIMS.md` with no reader left pointing at it.
- Test: `scripts/agents/board-check.test.mjs` (a folder fixture, a malformed file, 16 files over the limit) and a real two-branch merge shown in the PR body.
- Gate: this touches `scripts/agents/**` and `docs/agents/**`, so it needs two counted reviews, one of them a `security` lens. Karma approves and merges (CR-70, CR-73); a change to the claim rules is Karma's to approve.

## Split of the proposed group rows, batch 1 (21 Nov 2026, proposed)

Written 21 Nov 2026 by the product agent, docs only. Gate G0 is met only when a P0 row has a row of its own, and 683 of the 1,052 P0 rows map only to the proposed group rows filed from `docs/product/prd/BACKLOG-GAPS.md` (many of them size L). These 25 rows (BL-1158 to BL-1182) split eleven of those groups into rows of 2 to 6 P0 ids each, one PR per row: the first-run groups NS-39 to NS-45, then NS-33, NS-36, NS-08 (flip build), NS-09 and NS-14, and the stragglers of NS-19, NS-21, NS-24, NS-35 and NS-37. Each id on a Satisfies line below is one that only a group row named before; the group row itself is not edited by this batch. The count of every group, the split proposed for each and the later batches are in `docs/product/P0-SPLIT-PLAN-21nov.md`.

Every row is `proposed`: Karma or the founder sets `ready`. Dependencies are the group row's, unchanged; a wait on a founder step is carried by the row it depends on. Nothing here copies or changes a requirement. Ids come from `node scripts/agents/next-id.mjs` (develop plus open PRs, 21 Nov: BL-1158 was the next free id).

## Split of the proposed group rows, batch 2 (21 Nov 2026, proposed)

Written 21 Nov 2026 by the product agent, docs only, on `develop` `0ee5339`. These 26 rows (BL-1300 to BL-1325) split seven more of the proposed group rows filed from `docs/product/prd/BACKLOG-GAPS.md` into rows of 1 to 7 P0 ids each, one PR per row: BL-298 (NS-49, FR-PHS, FR-OPP), BL-296 (NS-47, FR-CUL), BL-182 (NS-17, FR-LOC), BL-187 (NS-38, FR-CMP), BL-295 (NS-46, NS-50, FR-DAY), BL-297 (NS-48, FR-NTC) and BL-127 (NS-03). A row holds at most 8 ids and at most 6 of them card rows, and the ids that share a test file or a screen stay together. Each id on a Satisfies line below is one that only a group row named before; the group rows themselves are not edited by this batch and stay as they are until every id of a group has a split row and product sets it `superseded`. The count per group and the later batches are in `docs/product/P0-SPLIT-PLAN-21nov.md`.

Every row is `proposed`: Karma or the founder sets `ready`. Owner and Depends on are the group row's, unchanged; two rows that may touch `supabase/` (the migration lint of BL-1307, the held-draft sync rule of BL-1313) add the data architect, and none of the 26 rows adds a migration. A step that needs the founder, counsel or a native reviewer is named in the row as outside it and stays in `docs/FOUNDER_TASKS.md`. Nothing here copies, weakens or changes a requirement. Ids come from `node scripts/agents/next-id.mjs` (develop plus open PRs, 21 Nov: BL-1300 was the next free id).

## Split of the proposed group rows, batch 4 (21 Nov 2026, proposed)

Written 21 Nov 2026 by the product agent, docs only, stacked on the fix PR for the #1236 reviews. These 36 rows (BL-1366 to BL-1401) split the four `pair` group rows filed from `docs/product/prd/BACKLOG-GAPS.md` that the 20 Nov plan put in batch 4, the last 218 P0 ids that had no row of their own: BL-126 (43 ids on the photo, share and keeping cards, BL-1366 to BL-1373), BL-045 (22 ids of the photo moments card, BL-1374 to BL-1377), BL-046 (13 ids of the pictures and videos card, BL-1378 to BL-1380) and BL-047 (140 function-file ids that the 20 Nov reviews added for the two photo cards, BL-1381 to BL-1401). A row holds at most 8 function ids (6 where the ids are card rows), and ids that share a function file or a card topic stay together. Each id on a Satisfies line below is one that only a group row named before; every one of the 218 appears on exactly one split row. The four group rows are set `superseded` because every id they list now has a split row.

The plan said these rows are written in a session with the founder. This run had none: the product agent wrote them alone from the cards and function reviews, so every row stays `proposed` (Mode `pair`, the group row's Owner and Depends on kept) and the founder reads them in a session before anyone sets one `ready`. The first step of each BL-126 row is a test, because whether the code already does each id was not checked here (the plan's [U]); a row whose ids are all proven becomes a docs-only Satisfies edit. Every photo-moments and media row is behind a flag that is off in every store build, waits for the device spike (Q-PM-7) and, where it names one, for a founder ruling (Q-PM-2 plan limits, Q-PM-3 whether media reaches our servers, Q-NTC-10 and Q-NTC-11 for Karma). Founder, counsel and device steps are named in the rows as outside them and stay in `docs/FOUNDER_TASKS.md` and on the founder device run sheet `docs/qa/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md`. No row adds a migration (`supabase/**` is a founder-only path; a server change would be its own row for the data architect). Nothing here copies, weakens or changes a requirement. Ids: BL-1366 was the first free id after BL-1365 on 21 Nov (open pull requests read by REST, 180 patches scanned for BL-1359 and above, no hit; `next-id.mjs` does not work in this environment).

#### BL-1424 Sign-out clears the join wait, so the next account's welcome cannot show the previous child's name
- Status: done (PR #1317 merged as `6f607d27f`). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer (auth). Milestone: M12. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: High until reproduced (privacy: a child's name staying in memory across accounts). The leak is in memory only: the store is never written to disk, so it ends when the app process ends. Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given (the child-name rule in `CLAUDE.md` Privacy rules is the nearest; no requirement id was checked).
- Problem and evidence: found by Lens B on #1289. `joinWait` is a module-level store (`apps/mobile/src/components/family/join-wait.logic.ts:123`) that holds `{ childId, name, since }`. Its only `clear()` calls are in `join-wait.tsx:40` and `:43`, which run only while the welcome's `useWelcomeJoinWait` hook is mounted. Nothing under `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth` calls `joinWait.clear()` (searched `apps/mobile/src`: `joinWait` appears only in `components/family/join-wait*` and `app/invite/index.tsx:40,174,177`). `session-provider.tsx` `signOut()` (`:559-564`) dispatches `SIGN_OUT_REQUESTED` and clears nothing of the wait. So if sign-out happens while no welcome hook is mounted, the name from the previous account stays in memory and could appear in the next account's welcome line (`joinWaitLine`). Whether the next welcome really reads it was not run: unverified.
- Scope: clear the join wait when the account signs out, for every sign-out reason (user, apple_revoked, force_reauth, switch_account), in the sign-out path rather than only in the welcome hook. No change to the wait's other rules.
- Done when: a test signs in as account A, starts a wait with a name, signs out with no welcome mounted, signs in as account B and reads no name (the wait is null); the test fails with the new clear removed.
- Test: `apps/mobile/test/join-wait.test.ts` plus an auth-side test. Depends on nothing else.

#### BL-1425 `pendingUploads()` treats a failed read as unsynced, with a typed result
- Status: done (PR #1319, 0e78228a7: `pendingUploads()` returns `{ kind: 'count', n } | { kind: 'unknown' }` and sign-out waits on unknown; tests `apps/mobile/test/auth-pending-uploads.test.ts` and `auth-sign-out-wait.test.ts`). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer (auth). Milestone: M12. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium. Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given.
- Problem and evidence: found by Lens A on #1273. `pendingUploads()` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/auth-store.ts:188-194` returns 0 when the probe throws, which tells sign-out nothing is waiting when the store could not be read. That is the opposite of fail-safe: sign-out could proceed and drop letters that were never uploaded. Its callers read a number: `apple-revocation.logic.ts:54-63`, `session-provider.tsx:299,316,374,560`, and the literal `pendingUploads: 0` at `:424` (switch_account, which never reads the probe), and the reducer's `waiting` line at `machine.logic.ts:195`. The 0 for "no sync engine registered" is correct and stays.
- Scope: return a typed result (for example `{ kind: 'count', n } | { kind: 'unknown' }`) and treat `unknown` as unsynced in the sign-out reducer and in the revocation and force-reauth paths, so sign-out waits as it does for a non-zero count. The way out of an endless wait is `cancelSignOutWait()` (`session-provider.tsx:566-568`, which dispatches `SIGN_OUT_WAIT_CANCELLED`); keep it reachable when the result is `unknown`. `unknown` never reaches a dispatch as `pendingUploads: 0`: every dispatch site above either passes the typed result on or treats it as unsynced; the `:424` literal is reviewed and either kept with a comment saying why or routed through the same read. The sync side's own `countOr0` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/sync/index.ts:61-67`, for the status line) is a separate read and is not changed here.
- Done when: a test with a probe that throws shows sign-out waiting, not completing; a test with no probe still shows 0 pending; every caller above compiles against the typed result.
- Test: `apps/mobile/test` auth and revocation tests. Unverified: how #1273 reshapes the probe; rebase on it if it has merged.

#### BL-1428 BL-458 part 3: how the Book catches an `entries` event between its first read and its subscribe
- Status: done (PR #1450 merged as `bacc1aa3e`; option B, as ruled in CR-145: one extra read in the effect after subscribing). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer (P5: letter page, Book, Recently deleted). Milestone: M4. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Council ruling (21 Nov 2026, CR-145): option B, one extra read in the effect. CPO for B; the CDO preferred A. The row owner picks and Karma ruled B, so the mobile engineer builds B and records it here. A mount-time list read is the cost named in the options; the test must show an `entries` event between the initialiser read and the subscribe is picked up.
- Priority: Low. Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given.
- Problem and evidence: BL-458 point 3. The Book reads its letters in the `useState` initialiser and subscribes in an effect, so an `entries` event between the two is missed until the next event (BL-458 Problem (3); unverified on a device). BL-458 stays `partly done` after #1287 merges; this row is the open part.
- Options for the mobile engineer: (A) a store change counter: the store increments a number on every `entries` event; the Book records the number at its initial read and, in the effect, compares it and re-reads on a difference. Trade-off: one small addition to the store's public surface and a counter every subscriber could misuse, but one cheap integer compare and no extra read when nothing changed. (B) one extra read in the effect: after subscribing, read the list again and set state only if it differs from the initialiser's. Trade-off: no store change and the smallest diff, but a full list read on every Book mount, which costs more for a large book, and a "differs" compare that has to be cheap and correct.
- Scope: decide A or B, record the choice in this row, then implement it in the same PR.
- Done when: the chosen option is written here; a test shows an `entries` event between the initialiser read and the subscribe is picked up at once.
- Test: `apps/mobile/test/p5-critics.test.ts` or a new Book test.

#### BL-1430 If the second prime becomes eligible after Yes and then reminders off, is that intended
- Status: done (PR #1419 merged as `9e8eb5e23`, council ruling CR-145). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer (asks). Milestone: M12. Size: XS. Depends on: none (PR #1274 has merged).
- Council ruling (21 Nov 2026, CR-145): a person who ever said Yes to the reminder prime is never primed again, kept as a device-only boolean (layer L2, no server field, nothing in analytics). For: Privacy, Design. Against: CPO and CDO, who would keep the behaviour. Karma broke the tie. Subject to F13 6.2 B row 4c (`docs/prd/v2/features/F13*.md`): the spec wins, and if row 4c reads against this the builder stops and files the conflict instead of building. Scope becomes the rule plus a `test/next-ask.test.ts` case named for it; no D-### proposal is needed beyond CR-145.
- Priority: Low. Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given (C-REQ-001 Rev allows at most two primes; read it before deciding).
- Problem and evidence: Lens B on #1274. The second-prime rule now exists on `develop` (PR #1274): `apps/mobile/src/lib/asks/next-ask.logic.ts:75` returns `reminder_prime` when `!firstLetter && firstMonthDone && primesShown === 1 && primeAllowed(primesShown) && !remindersOn`, with the cap `MAX_REMINDER_PRIMES = 2` at `:20`. `primesShown` counts showings from any source and does not record whether the person said Yes, so someone who said Yes to the first and later turned reminders off in Settings becomes eligible once the first month is done. Whether that matches F13 6.2 B row 4c was not checked. Considerations, not a decision: it would be a second, single, dismissible ask inside the cap; a person who turned reminders off on purpose may read it as being asked again. The founder decides.
- Scope: record the decision as a D-### proposal in the PR body and either keep the behaviour with a test that names it, or add a rule that a person who ever said Yes is never primed again, with its test.

#### BL-1466 Erase everything: a failed backup delete must not leave the export ZIP, recovery ZIP, print PDF or frame copies on disk
- Status: proposed (found by the NS-36 B5-4 test; Karma sets it to ready). Mode: agent. Owner: mobile engineer. Milestone: M12. Size: XS. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium (privacy: copies of a family's letters survive an Erase everything until a retry succeeds). Gate: none.
- Satisfies: none given (the nearest is the erase promise in `docs/legal/DELETION_AND_EXPORT_SPEC.md`; no requirement id was checked).
- Problem and evidence: `eraseDeviceFiles()` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/erase-everything.ts` holds the days-file failure as `daysLeft` and throws it last (line 101), but throws the held `backupFailure` at line 82, right after the recordings loop and before `removeWholeFrameCopies(0)` (line 83), the pictures folder delete (lines 88-89) and the `CACHE_COPIES` loop (lines 93-99: `exports`, `recovery-export`, `Print`, the picker cache and the baked cache). So when the backup file will not delete, those folders stay until a later retry succeeds. The mark stays set, so the retry does finish them (the green test `[NS-36-B5-4] what is green today` in the same file shows it); the gap is the window before the retry.
- Scope: hold `backupFailure` as `daysLeft` is held and throw it after the cache loop, after `daysLeft` is handled (decide which of the two is thrown if both fail, and say so in a comment). The order of the steps does not change.
- Done when: the test `it.fails('[NS-36-B5-4] the backup file will not go: ...')` in `apps/mobile/test/erase-all.test.ts` (line 1606) is changed to a plain `it` and passes, and the green test beside it still passes. Acceptance names that test to flip.
- Test: `apps/mobile/test/erase-all.test.ts`.

#### BL-1470 Sampling can drop an analytics event that must never be sampled
- Status: proposed (TRACKING_PLAN 5.3). Mode: agent. Owner: analytics engineer. Milestone: M12. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium (events that carry consent, letter saving, errors and the rest of the never-sampled list would be missing from counts if a rate below 1 were ever configured). Today no code sets `sampleRates` for them, which is unverified beyond `packages/analytics/src`; the risk is a future setting, not a current loss.
- Satisfies: FR-DAT-36 as the test cites it (its own row is about the allowlist, per the test comment); TRACKING_PLAN 5.3.
- Problem and evidence: `track()` in `packages/analytics/src/client.ts:170-175` applies `options.sampleRates?.[name]` to every event name and returns `dropped_sampled`, with no exemption. The test `packages/analytics/test/p0-never-sampled.test.ts` builds the P0 list as `analytics_opted_in`, `letter_saved` and every catalogue event whose `area` is capture, family, languages, reminders, plus, settings, children or errors (47 events today; I ran the file on `develop`, 96 tests pass). For each at rates 0 and 0.5 it asserts, in an `it.fails` per case (94 of them), that `track` returns a string other than `dropped_sampled` across 12 analytics ids. It is a red-pinned gap written as green: all 94 pass only because the assertion fails today. One control (`screen_view` at rate 0 is `dropped_sampled`) is a plain `it`, as are the list-size checks. It does not cover events from an area outside that list, or whether `sample_pct` is set for them.
- Scope: in `client.ts`, ignore `sampleRates` for the P0 set. Derive the set from the catalogue (not a second hand-kept list) so a new event in those areas is covered; the rule in the code and the test must come from the same place.
- Done when: all 94 `it.fails` cases in that file are plain `it` (the comment in the file says to remove `.fails` in the fixing PR) and pass; the `screen_view` control still passes.
- Test: `packages/analytics/test/p0-never-sampled.test.ts`.

- Status: proposed (docs/qa/test-plan-b13 risk 11). Mode: agent. Owner: analytics engineer. Milestone: M12. Size: S. Depends on: none.
- Priority: Medium (nothing in the catalogue breaks the promise today, the control test says the real catalogue passes; the guard would not stop someone adding a hash, file name, album, picture count or Photos permission). Gate: none.
- Satisfies: FR-DAT-36 and TRACKING_PLAN 6.2 and 6.3 as the test cites them (not re-read here).
- Problem and evidence: `packages/analytics/test/catalog.test.ts:19` has `FORBIDDEN_KEY = /(text|transcript|name|note|email|audio_url|birth|due_date|dob|token|query|phone|address|signs_as|language_code|locale|timezone|photo_url|word$|term$)/`, and line 64 allows an int up to 1000. `packages/analytics/test/allowlist-guards-narrow.test.ts` reads that guard and proves, in `it.fails` cases, what it does not reject: g1 hash, file and path, size and length, and library words as keys (4 cases); g2 `photo_count: int(0, 50)`; g3 a Photos permission enum (`full`, `limited`, `denied`); g4 an int limit above 100. All pass today because they assert the guard is wider than it is.
- Scope: widen the guard in `catalog.test.ts` (the key words, a rule for photo counts and the Photos permission, and an int limit of 100 or less), after checking the real catalogue still passes it; if an existing event needs more than 100 it is named in the PR and the founder decides. Test-file work only unless a catalogue entry fails the wider rule. The same PR flips the tests below.
- Done when: the four `it.fails` cases `[FR-DAT-36-g1]` (four key-word groups, one case each), `[FR-DAT-36-g2]`, `[FR-DAT-36-g3]` and `[FR-DAT-36-g4]` in `allowlist-guards-narrow.test.ts` are plain `it` and pass, and the control `[FR-DAT-36-ctl]` still passes. Acceptance names those tests to flip.
- Test: `packages/analytics/test/catalog.test.ts`, `packages/analytics/test/allowlist-guards-narrow.test.ts`.
